en: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed in clean, stagnant water, so emptying unused tires and bottles prevents dengue fever.
Washing a dog bite wound with soap and water for fifteen minutes significantly reduces the risk of rabies infection.
Raw chicken often contains Salmonella bacteria, so you must cook it completely and wash your hands to avoid food poisoning.
Looking directly at the sun during a solar eclipse can permanently damage the retina in your eyes.
The leaves of the oregano plant contain compounds that help soothe coughs and clear mucus from your respiratory tract.
Handling stray cats requires washing hands afterward because their fur can carry ringworm fungi that cause itchy skin rashes.
Drinking plain water instead of sugary sodas prevents tooth decay because sugar feeds the bacteria that destroy tooth enamel.
Planting trees like the Narra around your school filters dust from the air and provides cooling shade during hot afternoons.
Melanin is a pigment in your skin that absorbs ultraviolet radiation to protect your cells from sun damage.
Your brain consolidates newly learned information into long-term memory during the deep sleep stages of your nightly rest cycle.
Pigs can carry the Taenia solium tapeworm, so eating undercooked pork can cause a painful intestinal infection called taeniasis.
The seeds of apples contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide when chewed, so you should always spit out or avoid crushing them.
